claims.claim: A recent update removed anti-cheat support for Linux and Steam Deck, rendering the game unplayable on those platforms.

citations.review_text: Linux no longer works as it is blocked by ubisoft.

My 1.1 Hours was a few rounds with a friend after setting up options and controls.  Even though the game ran beautifully and i didn't have any issues inside of the game, it's simply not for me.  I don't have much to say about this title, but a lot more about the company behind it.

As of a recent update about a month ago of this writing.  Linux users are unable to play For Honor on their PC's because of Ubisoft's decision to remove their anti-cheat support for the OS.  This is not a Linux problem, this is an Ubisoft problem, as other anti-cheats work perfectly fine on Linux.  It's a shame, really.  They have great games, but they gate-keep too hard by controlling how they allow you to play them.  Their piss poor company choices with license revocation, DRM, and ecosystem dependence just leaves a bad taste in my mouth, as there's only victims with this setup.

I wrote this review mainly to add to the awareness that gamers should have the option to play any game they want on any platform they want without annoying launchers, license checks, and other BS that negatively impacts the gamer.  Ubisoft restricts you, therefore Ubisoft doesn't deserve you.

For those who do enjoy this game and don't care about Ubisoft's business practices, cool.  I'm glad you're having a good time with the title.  We're gamers, we're in the same boat, we're all in this together, and what matters most is that you're happy with your time spent on your favorite games; no if's, and's or but's.  We deserve it.  

Enjoy your time with any Ubisoft title as best and as much as you can.  That time is finite.  One day you'll login into their launcher and the game is gone.
Removing linux support is insane, can't even launch the game offline.

Fun Game, Cool Characters, Sword go bonk.

WHERE IS MY LINUX SUPPORT. IT WAS HERE. IT WORKED.

Fun game, dont give Ubisoft your money tho.
Love the game, played a ton on gamepass but they stopped linux support, which is a very weird decision, given its not a dedicated port.
while I did not really enjoy the game due to ubisoft launcher, removing linux and SD support made it even worse.

Can't run this on Deck, can't run this on my PC, and this only because Ubisoft couldn't just leave a 10-years old game the fuck alone.

It was working fine before, so give it back.
Removed linux support out of no where.

I had already owned this game for a while but didn't actually try it despite buying it, until recently. I already knew about the news of Ubisoft intentionally blocking Linux, so I intentionally downloaded and installed 120GB to my machine just so I could write this review, because I hadn't played the game with this account before they blocked Linux.
Now, finally, I want to say thank you Ubisoft for publicly shaming yourselves. We won't be updating our reviews until you change your mind, but it's not like we need you to do so anyways. Thank you for making me waste my money.

If you are one of those Windows users trying to ragebait by saying nobody uses Linux and whatnot: We don't have time for you, and we don't care neither about you nor your system. We don't care that you don't care about it the same way.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that matchmaking frequently pairs players against opponents of much higher skill levels.

citations.review_text:
I absolutely recommend this game! The story is awesome, the graphics are great, the characters are all so different from each other and there is something for absolutely everyone. However I will not deny that this game is difficult, it takes a good amount of getting used to to finally understand the mechanics. Even with 30 hours, I'm still learning and advancing in something new every time I play.


But then why are people talking about this game like it's the equivalent of sucking on Satan's quilled nutsack while being butt fucked by a red hot poker? I assume its because the online matches are genuine torture, there is an ABSURD amount of people who are CRAZY good at the game, and ! will admit that is not very fair on new players, but its not something to toss the whole game over. This game has an unbelievably high skill ceiling. And the matchmaking isn't that awesome either, sometimes you can get a baby game, and other times you genuinely want to eat your desk. 

But honestly, please don't let these reviews and memes talk about how they want to divorce their wife over this game, it's honestly one of a kind and something that you should really consider if you like fighting games, mediaeval stuff and all kinds of fun juicy details about sword fighting!

Story 4/5
Combat: 4/5 
Graphics: Decent
PvP Difficulty 5/5
Price: Buy on sale only

I'm not particularly into hack and slash games so I only recommend you get this if you want to play the Story. It was good enough that I played it in all four difficulty levels. Realistic difficulty was great as it removes the hit indicator so you just rely on pattern recognition. Somehow this didn't really translate to PvP.

In 17 PvP Duels, I only won 3. Skill issue perhaps or maybe it's because the matchmaking seems to not be able to find players at a similar skill level as me, I kept encountering higher level profiles. Or maybe I just don't have enough hours yet. Only being able to win 20% of the time just isn't for me, it was pretty satisfying to even win a round given how hard it is though.
Hella toxic game, you will genuinely never get someone even remotely close to your skill level, you need at least 1000+ hours to be any good at this shitty ass game

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game's publisher removed support for Linux-based operating systems, rendering the game unplayable on Linux and Steam Deck.

citations.review_text:
I actually have more playtime than just Steam since I used to play with Ubisoft Connect as well. 

This game is great, but Ubisoft have done nothing to address actual cheating issues like lag-switching & auto-parry scripting; instead they've broken support for Steam Deck and Linux by "strengthening" the EAC under the guise of 'player safety'. Ubisoft doesn't care about player protection and comfort, or they would have done something about the constant derogatory, offensive, genuinely disgusting imagery people use as emblems in the game, which depends on the players to report - do Ubisoft's job for them. 

This game is great. The characters, gameplay, atmosphere is really unique and something I always want to come back to. But the game is impossible to come back to because it barely had a playerbase to begin with, and the people still playing are at a such higher skill level you just get stomped on no matter what. Ubisoft has only just made that issue worse by blocking their Linux & Steam Deck users, further shrinking the already pathetic playerbase size. 

EAC was already implmented and functioning while the game was available on Linux. Ubisoft didn't provide any evidence of wrongdoing from Linux/Steam Deck systems. They haven't done anything to fix the actual issues with the game, only worsened some of them.

Also worth noting that falsly advertising a product as compatible with a certain OS and then purposely breaking support is generally not legal, as has already been tried and tested with the OtherOS debacle.
No longer playable on Linux, way to further shrink an already small player base

I had a great time with For Honor and used to happily recommend it to friends. Then Ubisoft blocked Linux and that was it.

Ubisoft can call it an anti-cheat measure all they want. From my end, I bought a game that worked and they deliberately made it stop working. After that, I’d have a hard time trusting Ubisoft with another purchase.
Removed perfectly functioning support for Linux, so no Steam Deck/Machine/OS. Can't even start the game, so the game is 100% useless now. Won't buy from Ubisoft ever again.

This game was fine until they decided to pull support for Linux-based OSes so they can force you to install some kernelspace spyware and Denuvo DRM in the name of "security", because God forbid we use free and open operating systems. This is absolutely disgusting corporate greed and I'm infuriated that my purchase is now unusable. Thanks Ubislop and I hope you get utterly destroyed by the greater open source/reverse engineer/pirate community. Make a real anti-cheat.
Wanted to write a positive review about the game and how unique it is and it deserves more love. But the publisher decided to ruin their reputation more by removing playability on Linux.

single_points.text: One reviewer says servers kick you constantly from matches and typing harmless words in chat can result in a temporary ban without explanation or a way to appeal.

citation.review_text:
Servers are kicking you a lot from matches, sometimes while you start a match with friend whule you waiting and loading it can kick a friend out and 
You can write nothing bad in chat like a word or whatever and you get temp banned with no way to appeal it and they dont even tell you what triggered it

single_points.text: One reviewer says unlocking a new character took a lot of grinding simply using the steel currency system.

citation.review_text:
it had such an interesting and unique concept, but the devs made the actual experience such an unpleasant one. it's incredibly infuriating to play against the unbalanced cast full of gimmick-reliant power creeps. the one good thing about this game was the steel currency system but it took so much grinding simply to unlock a new character. on top of everything, i built my computer with this game in mind only last year and installed linux on it, only for linux support to be dropped out of nowhere.
this game is a shambling corpse of what could've been a fascinating idea
